q1: SELECT C.DEPT_NAME, AVG(I.SALARY) FROM COURSE AS C INNER JOIN DEPARTMENT AS D ON (C.DEPT_NAME = D.DEPT_NAME) INNER JOIN TEACHES AS T ON (C.COURSE_ID = T.COURSE_ID) INNER JOIN INSTRUCTOR AS I ON (D.DEPT_NAME = I.DEPT_NAME) GROUP BY C.DEPT_NAME HAVING AVG(I.SALARY) > 50000 AND COUNT(DISTINCT I.SALARY) = 4

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because the condition in the HAVING clause differs. Q1 checks for COUNT(DISTINCT I.SALARY) = 4, while Q2 checks for COUNT(DISTINCT I.SALARY) > 4. These conditions are not the same, as the first one is inclusive of 4 distinct salaries, while the second one excludes 4 distinct salaries.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when the count of distinct salaries in a department is exactly 4. In this case, Q1 will return the department, but Q2 will not.
